title: Size and timescale of epidemics in the SIR framework
experiment: Raising the threshold γ = β/α by doubling β or by halving α gives the same epidemic peak I*/N ≈ 0.30, but the peak arrives about twice as late when α is cut, which is the paper's scaling result t*(2) = t*(1)/λ (Eq. 23).
archetype_reason: the claim is about the time course of I(t) under the stated SIR ODEs (Eq. 1), and the metrics are the timing and height of the peak

fixed.model: classical SIR, Eq. 1: dS/dt = -α S I, dI/dt = α S I - β I, dR/dt = β I
fixed.step: one step = 1 day, integrated with RK4 using 10 substeps of 0.1 day
fixed.t_peak_definition: day index (0-based step count) at which I is largest over the run

source.quote: Here the parameter $\alpha$ corresponds to a contact rate (also called infection rate).
The parameter $\beta$ is a removal rate; more precisely, it is the inverse of the typical removal time

metrics.name: peak_frac
metrics.label: peak infected I*/N
metrics.meaning: maximum over all simulated days of I(t) divided by N

metrics.name: t_peak
metrics.label: peak day t*
metrics.meaning: the day (step index) at which I(t) attains its maximum over the run

metrics.name: final_frac
metrics.label: ever infected R/N
metrics.meaning: R(t)/N at the last simulated day

reproduce.claim: Doubling β (α unchanged) doubles γ, so the peak drops to I*/N ≈ 0.30 and arrives near day 41 (Table 1).

source.section: Epidemic management in the SIR framework
source.quote: Actions reducing $\gamma$ by the same factor through action on the different parameters produce the same epidemic peak level

contrast.claim: Halving α instead (β unchanged) gives the same γ, the same peak height and the same final size, but the peak comes about twice as late.

source.section: Scaling properties of the SIR equations
source.quote: increasing $\beta$ by a factor $\lambda$ , $t_{*}$ is reduced by a factor $1/\lambda$ , with respect to the value attained by reducing $\alpha$ .

fallback.title: Size and timescale of epidemics in the SIR framework
fallback.experiment: Raising the epidemic threshold γ lowers the closed-form peak I* = N − γ − γ log(N/γ) (Eq. 8), showing that the peak is a decreasing function of γ.
fallback.archetype_reason: the peak height is a closed-form function of γ alone, so one configuration gives one computed number

fixed.formula: I* = N − γ − γ ln(N/γ) when N > γ, else 0 (Eq. 8)
